0.0.n: Refers to the item the speaker is discussing.

0.1.n: Marks this item as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: A borrowed word followed by a number specifying the item's size.

0.3.n: Gives the size number, not the quantity of items.

0.4.n: The linking form of だ connects the size description to the age description.

0.6.n: Here, this age indicates when a baby can start using the item.

0.7.n: Marks the starting age, implying six months and older.

0.8.n: This linking form of だ comes before explanatory ん after the age description.

0.9.n: Short for の, it adds an explanatory tone rather than referring to a thing.

0.10.n: Makes the explanatory ending んです polite.

0.11.n: Introduces a contrast with the age range of the item currently in use.

1.1.n: Identifies Ellea as the person using the item.

1.2.n: Places the use of the item at the present time.

1.3.n: The て-form of 使う plus いる describes ongoing use and modifies もの.

1.4.n: Refers to the item described by エレアが今使っている.

1.5.n: Marks the entire phrase about Ellea's current item as the topic.

1.7.n: Gives the youngest age in the item's recommended range.

1.8.n: Marks the lower end of the age range; eighteen months is the upper end.

1.9.n: Gives the oldest age in the range; まで, meaning up to, is omitted here.

1.10.n: Connects the age range to もの, describing which ages the item is intended for.

1.11.n: Stands for an item intended for the stated age range.

1.12.n: The form of だ used after a noun before ので.

1.13.n: Presents the current item's age range as the reason for the speaker's decision.

2.0.n: Shows that the speaker's judgment about suitability was not certain.

2.1.n: Refers back to the size-two item.

2.2.n: Combines で and も to suggest that this alternative item could also work.

2.3.n: A conversational use of いける meaning something is suitable or workable, rather than physically able to go.

2.4.n: Marks the preceding idea as the content of the speaker's thought.

2.5.n: The て-form of 思う connects the speaker's judgment to the purchase that followed.

2.6.n: The polite past form of 買う describes a completed purchase.

0.lit: This, as for, is size two, and is from six months, you see, but…
0.tip: なんですけど adds an explanatory tone and politely leads into a contrast.

1.lit: As for the one Ellea is using now, because it is one for three months to eighteen months…
1.tip: Japanese puts the description before もの: エレアが今使っているもの means the one Ellea is using now.

2.lit: Probably even with this it will work, thinking that, I bought it.
2.tip: と marks what was thought, while 思って links that thought to the decision to buy.
